roster_note: type-design-analyzer gated out (has_new_types=false); pr-test-analyzer dispatched (diff touches lib/test/modules/efficiency-trace-telemetry.sh and adds testable logic in lib/efficiency-trace.sh). Shadow ignores iterations:first-only, so full expected roster dispatched.

phase3_findings.description: Shadow path (shadow-review.md) does not explicitly classify a wrong-type (non-array) expected_reviewers as malformed, unlike Step 1 (loop-control.md) which rejects a 'wrong-type or empty report'. In practice still fails closed (a non-array operand cannot satisfy the always-on-floor coverage check, routing to outcome-3 shortfall), so no clean-verdict leak. Worth one clause mirroring Step 1's wrong-type wording for symmetry.

Step 1 inline (unavailable) arm does not restate that expected_reviewers must be recorded on that path; it relies on the global 'written on every iteration' statement and shadow-review.md's 'on the inline path the parent evaluates the same Phase 3.1 gates directly'. Documentation-completeness nit, not a missing producer.

The non-empty-array well-formedness contract for expected_reviewers lives entirely in agent-executed skill prose; efficiency-trace.sh --self-check is presence-only. This is the documented design gap (review pass is the compensating control), not a defect to close. A reader should not mistake the green suite as covering the non-empty-array contract.

No positive check that the complete fixture exercises the zero-warning path with a populated (non-empty) roster; the fixture carries expected_reviewers:[]. Very low-value hardening since --self-check has no type awareness today.

Shadow guard keeps four always-on as unconditional floor; empty/sub-floor roster is outcome-3 shortfall, never vacuous full. loop-control.md two paragraphs agree. All four carriers consistent. No silent failures or unjustified fallbacks introduced.
